assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Abbott India (standalone; no subsidiaries; FY = April-March, ₹ crore). One reported segment, so the engine runs one revenue-growth path and one EBITDA-margin path; the business-line build (own brands vs Novo Nordisk partner brands) sits in `businessLines` and the authoring script checks that it sums to model revenue. Other income = treasury yield x opening net cash on the company's basis (cash + all bank term deposits incl. those over 12 months, less lease liabilities: Rs4,238 cr at Mar-26) + recurring non-treasury income. Valued on P/E, as the street does.
assumptions._revenueWhy: Built by business (see businessLines; the script checks the sum). FY27E +5.75%: own brands +11% (Q1FY27 ~+11% on Pharmarack; IQVIA ~12% for the June quarter; most power brands +10-12%; Thyronorm +12.7%, Cremaffin Plus +19.8%, Vertin +18.3%, Influvac +25.2% on MAT Jul-26, but Udiliv +3%, Digene -1%, Duphaston +6% (Pharmarack); price growth limited: NLEM ceiling +0.65% from Apr-2026 on ~26% of the own portfolio) and Novo partner brands -4% (cartridge and pen insulins discontinued from 2025, Mixtard -31% and Rybelsus -16% on MAT Jul-26, partly offset by Extensior from Mar-2026). Q1FY27 was +4.3%; Q2-Q4 at the Q1 run-rate with normal seasonality gives ~Rs7,320 cr. FY28E +7.8%: own +10.5%, partner +2% (Extensior volume, Novo decline annualised). FY29E +7.9%: own +10%, partner +3%. Below the street (BOBCAPS +8% FY27E, ICICI Direct +8%) because we take the Q1 partner decline as lasting.

businessLines._why: Company does not split revenue. FY26 base = 65% own brands / 35% Novo partner brands (BOBCAPS Q4FY26 review: core portfolio 65% of sales; BOBCAPS 3-Sep-2026: in-licensed Novo portfolio 35% of sales; company split FY21-24 was 64-66% / 34-36%). Own brands include services income from Abbott affiliates (Rs81 cr).

assumptions._marginWhy: EBITDA before other income: 26.4% (FY25), 27.3% (FY26), 28.8% in Q1FY27 (gross margin +283bp to 48.6% as low-margin partner sales fell and own brands grew). Mix does most of the work: BOBCAPS puts the core portfolio's EBITDA margin at 41.8% (Q4FY26) against a distribution margin of a few per cent on Novo products, so each point of mix shift adds ~0.4pp. FY27E 28.5%: Q1 28.8%, with Q3 carrying the annual salary cycle (Q3FY26 26.9%) and FY26's labour-code charge (Rs18 cr) not repeating. FY28E 29.0% and FY29E 29.5%: own brands rise from 68% to 71% of revenue; we hold the own-brand margin roughly flat (more launches, field-force investment). BOBCAPS models 28.2/29.2/30.3%, ICICI Direct 27.6/28.1%.
assumptions._capexWhy: Cash capex Rs53 cr (FY25) and Rs41 cr (FY26) plus right-of-use additions (Rs169 cr in FY25 for a new office lease, Rs15 cr in FY26); capital commitments only Rs0.5 cr at Mar-26 (AR FY26 note 37). We use Rs60-65 cr a year including lease additions.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation Rs76 cr (PPE Rs28.7 cr, intangibles Rs2.9 cr, right-of-use Rs44.4 cr); Q1FY27 Rs19.8 cr (Rs79 cr annualised). Rate chosen so FY27E depreciation is ~Rs80 cr on the engine's gross block (CWIP held flat).

otherTreasury._why: Company treasury at Mar-26 = cash and equivalents Rs442.33 cr + term deposits of 3-12 months Rs1,790.00 cr + term deposits with more than 12 months to maturity Rs2,178.00 cr (non-current other financial assets) = Rs4,410.33 cr (AR FY26 notes 6, 10, 11). Screener counts Rs2,254.95 cr as cash (incl. Rs21.28 cr earmarked for unpaid dividends and Rs1.34 cr of margin money) and puts the long deposits in other assets. Adjustment = 2,178.00 - 21.28 - 1.34 = +Rs2,155.38 cr, so the model's opening treasury equals the company's Rs4,410 cr; less Rs172 cr of lease liabilities (Screener borrowings) = Rs4,238 cr of net cash. Interest accrued on deposits (Rs139 cr) is left out.

assumptions._treasuryWhy: FY26 interest on fixed deposits Rs256.75 cr on average deposits and cash of Rs4,098 cr (Mar-25 Rs3,785 cr, Mar-26 Rs4,410 cr) = 6.27% (AR FY26 notes 10-12, 25). Deposits were placed when the repo rate was 6.5%; it was 5.25% when the RBI held it on 5-Aug-2026, so the yield drifts down as one-to-two-year deposits roll over: 6.0% in FY27E, 5.75% after. Applied to opening net cash (the engine has no intra-year timing; the Rs1,394 cr FY26 dividend leaves in Aug-2026 and the engine deducts the FY27 dividend instead, of similar size).
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Recurring non-treasury other income (AR FY26 note 25): steady items ~Rs3 cr (interest on security deposits Rs1.1 cr, rent from an affiliate Rs1.2 cr, other interest and miscellaneous Rs0.7 cr) plus lumpy liabilities written back and insurance/carrier claims (Rs14.8 cr in FY25, Rs12.0 cr in FY26), of which we take about half: ~Rs10 cr a year. Left out as one-offs (Rs16.4 cr in FY26): interest on an income-tax refund Rs10.6 cr, gain on selling two Mumbai offices Rs4.1 cr, exchange gain Rs1.6 cr. FY27E total other income ~Rs264 cr vs Rs288 cr in FY26 and Rs291 cr in the twelve months to Jun-26: the gap is the one-offs, half the lumpy items and the lower deposit yield (6.0% vs 6.27%).
assumptions._interestLabel: Finance cost (interest on lease liabilities, unwinding of provisions)
assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 Rs25.0 cr = lease interest Rs18.0 cr (Rs125 cr of the Rs172 cr lease liability is to Abbott Healthcare for office space) + other Rs2.7 cr + unwinding of provisions Rs4.3 cr; Q1FY27 Rs5.9 cr. Falls as the lease liability amortises. No borrowings.
assumptions._taxWhy: Effective rate 25.4% in FY26 (25.7% before Rs6.8 cr of prior-year credits) and 25.1% in Q1FY27; new-regime 25.17% plus disallowances.
assumptions._payoutWhy: Total payout (final + special) 84.6% / 73.2% / 72.7% / 72.5% / 71.4% / 89.8% in FY21-26: average 77%; the final dividend alone has been ~72% for three years and specials come irregularly (FY26 Rs131 a share). No target payout is disclosed. We use 80%. Timing: the engine deducts each year's dividend in that year; in reality it is paid in August of the next year, so FY27's engine outflow (~Rs1,390 cr) stands in for the Rs1,394 cr FY26 dividend actually paid in Aug-2026.

dcf._betaWhy: Debt-free, cash-rich, India-only branded pharma with an MNC parent: defensive earnings. We keep 0.8 (Ke 11.3%), the same as the other pharma initiations, rather than a lower beta that would flatter the DCF.
dcf._tgWhy: 6%: the Indian pharma market grows ~9-10% in value; Abbott's own brands grow with it, the partner business slower; a long-run nominal rupee growth of 6% is below both.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~8% to 8% (own brands ~10%, partner brands low single digits, mix shifting to own brands).
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: Margin creeps from 29.5% to 30% on mix; no further expansion is assumed (reinvestment in launches and field force).
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex ~1% of revenue (incl. right-of-use additions; FY24-26 average ~0.8% plus leases); depreciation 1.1% of revenue (FY26 1.1%).

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Own brands keep growing at 12-13% (IPM in double digits, Thyronorm, Cremaffin, Vertin, Arachitol and the 75 planned launches), Extensior and Ryzodeg stabilise the partner business, and mix lifts margins faster.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Novo shrinks its Indian portfolio further or ends the arrangement, generics erode Duphaston and Udiliv, and price control caps Thyronorm; revenue grows ~3% a year and margins stall.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How the street values Abbott India: P/E (BOB Capital Markets 32x Sep-28E EPS, 3-Sep-2026; ICICI Direct 36x FY28E, 13-Aug-2026; ICICI Securities 38x FY27E, Nov-2025). 40x = Abbott's 36.1x median one-year-forward P/E since Apr-2021 (house forwardMedian on reported EPS; exceptional items are immaterial, so the pre-exceptional median is also 36.1x; no trough years: forward EPS was never below 108.3% of its prior three-year peak) times the pharma sector factor of 1.1025 (median of SUNPHARMA, DIVISLAB, TORNTPHARM, ZYDUSLIFE, CIPLA, AUROPHARMA, ALKEM, IPCALAB trailing P/E at the 30-Sep close vs their five-year medians: +10.25%, PLAYBOOK §7c; our reproduction +10.25%) = 39.8x, rounded to the nearest half-turn. No blend with Abbott's own de-rating (−25.6%) and no growth adjustment (sensitivity rows only). Bull 43x (75th percentile 39.1x x factor); bear 37.5x (25th percentile 34.1x x factor).

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Counts net cash at face value and ignores other income. Abbott's own trailing EV/EBITDA since Apr-2021 (market value less company net cash incl. long deposits, over operating EBITDA before other income; Screener's series includes other income and ignores long deposits) has a median of 36.0x; times the EV/EBITDA analogue of the sector factor (+9.1%, same eight peers) = 39.3x, rounded to 39.5x and applied to trailing EBITDA at the target date (half FY27E + half FY28E) plus net cash at Sep-2027. Bull 41.5x / bear 37x (75th / 25th percentile x factor).

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 15-year FCFF at an 11.3% cost of equity, terminal growth 6%, plus net cash.

cover.headline: A quality franchise de-rated while pharma re-rated: on the street's P/E method and its own history Abbott India has {{dcf.upside|chg}} upside; the DCF is the caution
cover.lead: Abbott India is the largest listed Indian subsidiary of a foreign drug maker: 75% owned by Abbott Laboratories, ₹6,929 cr of FY26 revenue, two-thirds from its own brands (Thyronorm, Udiliv, Duphalac, Cremaffin, Duphaston, Vertin) at a ~40% EBITDA margin and one-third from Novo Nordisk insulin and diabetes brands it distributes for a thin margin. It pays no royalty to its parent, has no debt and ₹4,238 cr of net cash. Q1FY27 revenue rose only 4.3% as Novo brands fell, but own brands grew ~11%, gross margin rose 283bp and profit 17%. At ₹27,125 the stock is 22% below its Jun-2025 peak (weekly close) and trades at 30.0x Sep-28E EPS against a 36.1x forward median since 2021, while pharma peers trade 10.25% above their own medians. The street values Abbott on **P/E (32-38x)**. We forecast EPS of ₹791 / 863 / 947 for FY27-29E, below consensus (₹903 for FY28E). Applying **40x to Sep-28E EPS of ₹905.0** (Abbott's 36.1x forward median × the pharma sector factor of 1.1025) gives **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with BUY.** Cross-checks: EV/EBITDA ₹42,946; DCF ₹21,835, which says the price already capitalises a lot. Bull {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.p: Own brands (~65% of revenue) grew ~11% in Q1FY27 and ~10% over the year to Jul-2026 (Pharmarack): Thyronorm +12.7%, Vertin +18%, Cremaffin Plus +20%, Influvac +25% (IQVIA). They earn ~40% EBITDA margins (BOBCAPS), use almost no capital and pay no royalty. The laggards are Udiliv, Digene and Duphaston (generic dydrogesterone). We model own brands at +11% / +10.5% / +10%.

arguments.h: The Novo third is shrinking: it hurts revenue more than profit
arguments.p: Novo Nordisk is discontinuing insulin cartridges and pens in India (Mixtard −31%), and semaglutide generics hit Rybelsus (−16%); Extensior (a second Ozempic brand) launched one month before the patent expired. Partner brands earn ~3-5% EBITDA margins, so they are ~35% of revenue but only ~4-6% of EBITDA. We model them at -4% / +2% / +3%: reported growth of +{{F.salesGrowth.0|pct}} / +{{F.salesGrowth.1|pct}} / +{{F.salesGrowth.2|pct}} with margins rising to {{F.ebitdaMargin.2|pct}}.

arguments.h: Cash-rich, asset-light, high payout; but the parent decides
arguments.p: Capex was ₹41 cr in FY26 against ₹1,319 cr of operating cash; 71-90% of profit is paid out (FY26: ₹656 a share incl. a ₹131 special) and deposits still grew to ₹4,410 cr. ROE is 34%. The catch: Abbott owns 75%, the free float trades ~US$3mn a day, there are no earnings calls and no split of own vs partner revenue.

arguments.h: Valuation: cheap on history, expensive on cash flows
arguments.p: Abbott's trailing P/E is −25.6% below its five-year median, the most de-rated name in the pharma set, and 31.4x FY28E vs a 36.1x forward median. Our house rule ignores that de-rating and the slower growth (EPS ~9% a year vs 18% in FY21-26), which gives 40x and {{dcf.tp|inr}}. On a DCF at an 11.3% cost of equity it is worth ₹21,835; on BOBCAPS' 32x, ₹28,960. The upside needs the market to pay its old multiple again.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): revenue growth with a full quarter of the Novo decline, margin, and other income after the ₹1,394 cr dividend paid in Aug-2026.
Monthly IQVIA / Pharmarack data: Udiliv and Duphaston vs the market; Thyronorm and Vertin; Extensior's share of the semaglutide generic market.
Novo Nordisk's Indian portfolio decisions (insulin formats, new products routed through Abbott) and any change to the arrangement.
FY27 dividend and any special dividend (May-2027); use of ₹4,400 cr of cash; any return of analyst meetings.
Price policy: April-2027 WPI-linked revision for NLEM drugs; any new NLEM list.

sections.title: A 75%-owned Abbott subsidiary selling trusted brands in India: two-thirds its own portfolio, one-third Novo Nordisk's insulin

blocks.p: Abbott India sells branded medicines in India (98.8% of revenue; exports to Sri Lanka, Nepal, Maldives and Bhutan are 1.2%). It is 75% owned by Abbott Laboratories of the US through three UK holding companies. Revenue was ₹6,929 cr in FY26 and comes from three streams. **Own brands (~65%)**: 140+ brands across gastro and liver (Udiliv, Duphalac, Cremaffin, Digene, Creon), thyroid (Thyronorm), women's health (Duphaston, Femoston), the nervous system (Vertin, Prothiaden), vitamin D (Arachitol) and vaccines (Influvac). Several are Abbott global brands (Abbott Laboratories names Creon, Duphaston, Femoston and Influvac among its key established-pharma brands), sold under marketing rights from Abbott affiliates for which **no price or royalty is paid**. **Novo Nordisk partner brands (~35%)**: Abbott distributes Novo's insulins (Mixtard, Ryzodeg, Actrapid and others), oral semaglutide (Rybelsus) and, since Feb-2026, Extensior, a second brand of semaglutide, and keeps a distribution margin. **Services to Abbott affiliates** (₹81 cr). Abbott India owns one plant (Goa); most products are bought in, from Novo, from Abbott group companies and from contract manufacturers: traded goods were 46% of FY26 revenue.

sections.title: From Boots (1944) to Knoll to Abbott: eight decades, one big merger (Solvay, 2011) and no dilution since

blocks.p: Abbott India began life as Boots Pure Drug Company (India) in 1944, became Knoll Pharmaceuticals when BASF bought Boots' drug business (1995), and passed to Abbott when Abbott bought Knoll worldwide (2001; renamed in 2002). Its portfolio took its present shape in 2011, when Solvay Pharma India (bought by Abbott globally in 2010) was merged into it, bringing Duphaston, Duphalac, Creon and Influvac. Abbott's other big Indian purchase, Piramal's domestic formulations business (2010), went into Abbott Healthcare Pvt Ltd, which is unlisted and 100% owned by the parent, so Abbott runs two branded-medicine businesses in India, only one of them listed. The share count has been 2.12 cr since 2011.

sections.title: The Indian drug market: ₹2.57 lakh crore, growing ~10% with regulated prices; GLP-1 generics and insulin exits reshape diabetes

blocks.p: India's domestic formulations market was worth ₹2,565 bn at chemist prices in FY26, up 9.9% (IQVIA). Abbott's own description: the market "has historically delivered 8-9% growth", volume growth is "moderate at 5-6%" and pricing is "stable and regulated". Growth picked up in 2026 (Q1FY27 ~13%, partly GLP-1 launches). Three forces matter for Abbott. (1) **Price control:** medicines on the National List of Essential Medicines (NLEM) may raise prices only by the wholesale-price index each April: +0.65% from 1-Apr-2026. Others may rise up to 10% a year. (2) **Diabetes is being reshaped:** semaglutide (Ozempic, Rybelsus) went off patent on 20-Mar-2026; 20+ companies launched generics and Novo cut prices by up to 48%. Novo is also winding down cartridge and pen insulins in India, a gap Biocon, Wockhardt, Eris and Lupin are filling. (3) **Generics of old brands:** cheaper copies press on established molecules (Abbott names dydrogesterone, the molecule in Duphaston).

blocks.p: For years Abbott grew at or above the market. FY26 revenue rose 8.1% against IPM growth of 9.9%, and Q1FY27 only 4.3% against ~12% IQVIA growth for its own brands. The difference is mostly the partner business: Novo's discontinued insulin formats and the fall in Rybelsus after semaglutide generics. The own portfolio is healthier: +10% on Pharmarack (MAT Jul-26) and ~+11% in Q1FY27, with CNS +15%, gastro +8% and women's health +8%. But that is market growth, not outperformance: the biggest brands (Udiliv, Digene, Duphaston) grow below the market.

sections.title: Novo Nordisk's brands: a third of revenue, a thin margin and a shrinking portfolio; Extensior arrived just before generics

blocks.p: Abbott India has marketed Novo Nordisk's insulin in India for decades (the human-insulin pact with Novo and Torrent dates back to the Boots/Knoll era; sources give 1987 or 1998). The arrangement was ~35% of revenue in FY21-24 (company split published by BOBCAPS: ₹1,535 cr in FY21, ₹2,048 cr in FY24) and is still ~35% (BOBCAPS, Sep-2026). Abbott buys the products and resells them for a distribution margin: BOBCAPS' core-portfolio figures imply a partner EBITDA margin of only ~3-5%, i.e. ~₹73-121 cr a year, 4-6% of EBITDA. Three things have changed since 2025. (1) In Apr-2025 Novo told Abbott it would discontinue Penfill and FlexPen insulins (Actrapid, Insulatard, Levemir, Xultophy) in India; Human Mixtard continues in vials. Mixtard fell 31% in the year to Jul-2026. (2) Semaglutide's patent expired on 20-Mar-2026: Rybelsus (oral semaglutide) fell 16% as generics arrived. (3) On 27-Feb-2026 Novo gave Abbott Extensior, a second brand of semaglutide (Ozempic) for diabetes, launched into the generic price war. Ryzodeg (+13%) is the one large Novo brand still growing.

sections.title: Dealings with Abbott: no royalty, ₹409 cr of purchases from a Swiss affiliate, and ₹757 cr of dividends a year to the parent

blocks.p: Many Indian subsidiaries of foreign drug makers pay a royalty or brand fee to the parent. Abbott India does not: the FY26 annual report says it "has access to marketing rights with the affiliates of the parent company for which no price is paid or payable" (the note names Abbott Healthcare Products BV and Abbott Biologicals BV, Netherlands). The money flows to the parent through three other channels. **Purchases:** ₹309 cr of raw materials and ₹100 cr of finished goods from Abbott Products Operations AG (Switzerland) in FY26 (₹533 cr in FY25); related parties supplied 12.43% of all purchases (15.64% in FY25). **Services with Abbott Healthcare Pvt Ltd** (the parent's unlisted Indian arm): Abbott India paid ₹74 cr for shared services, ₹69 cr of conversion (contract manufacturing) charges and ₹38 cr of office rent, and received ₹65 cr for services it provides. **Dividends:** ₹757 cr in FY26 (75% of the dividend).

But the parent controls the brands (marketing rights can be withdrawn or priced), decides which new Abbott products go to the listed company or to its 100%-owned Abbott Healthcare, and sets the payout. sections.title: Price control: about a quarter of the own portfolio is under NLEM, including all of Thyronorm; FY27's allowed increase is 0.65%

blocks.p: India caps the prices of medicines on the National List of Essential Medicines (NLEM) through the Drug Price Control Order (DPCO). The National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) sets a ceiling for each formulation and lets it rise each April by the wholesale-price index: +0.65% from 1-Apr-2026. Medicines outside the list may raise prices by up to 10% a year. At its last investor meet (Sep-2022) Abbott said ~26% of its own business by value is NLEM, and that its "entire range" of Thyronorm (12.5-150 mcg) is under price control. Human insulins (part of the Novo partner business) are also on the list. The only price-control liability on Abbott's books is a 1996 Drug Prices Equalisation Account claim (₹3.47 cr, under stay).

blocks.p: The moat is in the brands: Thyronorm, Udiliv, Duphalac, Cremaffin and Vertin have held leadership for years because doctors trust them and patients repeat them, and Abbott can sell them with almost no capital. That is why the business earns a 34% return on equity even with ₹4,400 cr of low-yielding cash, and a return on operating capital that is extremely high. The moat does not protect prices (price control, generics) and does not create new products; growth depends on market growth and on what the parent chooses to give the listed company.

blocks.callout: **Verdict:** narrow moat, wide returns. The brands justify a premium to generic-export pharma, but the absence of a pipeline and the dependence on the parent and Novo argue against paying for growth that is not there.

sections.title: Revenue +10% a year since FY21, EPS +18%: margins did the heavy lifting, and that tailwind is now mostly spent

blocks.p: Abbott India's revenue grew from ₹4,310 cr in FY21 to ₹6,929 cr in FY26, 10% a year, almost exactly the pace of the Indian drug market. Earnings grew much faster: EPS rose from ₹325 to ₹730 (18% a year). Two things explain the gap. First, the EBITDA margin (operating profit before other income) widened from 21.4% to 27.3% as Abbott's own brands grew faster than the low-margin Novo Nordisk insulin it distributes, and as employee and other costs grew slower than sales. Second, interest on a growing cash pile lifted other income from ₹81 cr to ₹288 cr. FY26 was the first sign of a slowdown: revenue +8.1%, EPS +9.7%, and Q1FY27 revenue grew only 4.3%.

sections.title: Capital allocation: almost no capex, 71-90% of profit paid out, and still ₹4,400 cr of cash

blocks.p: Abbott India needs very little capital. It owns one plant (Goa), buys most of what it sells from contract manufacturers and from Novo Nordisk, and spent only ₹41 cr on capex in FY26 against ₹1,319 cr of operating cash flow. So almost all profit is free cash. The company has paid out 71-90% of profit as dividends in each of the last six years: a regular final dividend of ~72% of EPS since FY24, plus special dividends in FY20-23 and FY26 (₹131 a share). Even so, bank deposits grew from ₹3,785 cr (Mar-25) to ₹4,410 cr (Mar-26), because interest received (₹385 cr in FY26) and ₹29 cr from selling two Mumbai offices more than covered the gap. Management describes capital allocation as "measured and consistent" and mentions "potential acquisitions", but we found no acquisition since the Solvay Pharma India merger (2011), and the FY25-26 cash-flow statements show none.

blocks.callout: **The capital question.** ₹4,410 cr of deposits is 7.7% of Abbott's market value and earns ~6% before tax (~4.5% after), well below the 34% ROE of the business. Minority shareholders cannot force a decision; the parent, with 75% of the shares and 75% of every dividend (₹757 cr in FY26), effectively sets the payout. We assume an 80% payout and no acquisition; a larger special dividend or a buyback would lift ROE but not EPS much.

sections.title: Earnings quality: clean accounts and strong cash conversion; watch sales-return provisions and the interest share of profit

bullets: **Revenue and returns.** Distributors may return goods that expire in the supply chain, so revenue is booked net of an estimated return provision: sales returns of ₹133 cr in FY26 (₹154 cr in FY25), 1.9% of contracted sales. The auditor (Walker Chandiok, Grant Thornton network) names this provision as the only key audit matter.

**Other income is 14% of profit before tax.** ₹257 cr of the ₹288 cr is deposit interest; ₹16.3 cr was one-off in FY26 (tax-refund interest, gain on selling two offices, exchange gain). We forecast only recurring items.

**Labour codes.** The new labour codes (notified 21-Nov-2025) added ₹18.1 cr to FY26 employee costs (gratuity ₹15.7 cr, leave ₹2.4 cr), booked in operating costs, not as an exceptional item; Q3FY26's margin (26.9%) carried it.
**Exceptional items** are immaterial (₹5 cr after tax in FY26 per Screener), so reported EPS is a fair basis for history and forecasts.

**Cash conversion.** Operating cash flow was ₹1,319 cr in FY26 (85% of profit) after ₹540 cr of tax; interest received sits in investing cash flow. Before tax, cash from operations was ~98% of EBITDA (Screener). FY25 (86%) was lower because inventory rose ₹262 cr.
**Share-based pay** is in Abbott Laboratories shares (₹12.7 cr charged in FY26); no dilution of Abbott India shares.
**Contingent liabilities** are small (₹114 cr: income tax ₹86 cr, sales tax ₹17 cr, customs ₹11 cr).

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: GREEN.** Conservative, simple accounts: no debt, no capitalised costs of note, no acquisitions, small contingencies, and profit that turns into cash. The two things to read carefully are the return provision (judgemental) and the large interest component of profit, which falls if the payout rises or deposit rates fall.

sections.title: Balance sheet: debt-free, ₹4,238 cr of net cash, and working capital funded by suppliers

blocks.p: At Mar-26 Abbott India had no borrowings; its only financial liability was ₹172 cr of leases (₹125 cr of it for offices rented from Abbott Healthcare). Against this it held ₹4,410 cr of cash and bank deposits: ₹442 cr of cash and short deposits, ₹1,790 cr of 3-12-month deposits and ₹2,178 cr of deposits maturing after more than a year, which Screener files under "other assets" (so its "cash" of ₹2,255 cr understates the true figure by half). Net cash was therefore ₹4,238 cr, ~₹1,995 a share. Working capital is lean: inventory of 94 days of cost is funded by 109 days of supplier credit, and customers pay in ~19 days.

sections.title: Our honest summary: a high-quality franchise at a de-rated price; the upside needs the market to pay its old multiple for slower growth

blocks.callout: **What you are buying:** India's largest listed MNC pharma franchise: trusted brands in thyroid, liver, gastro, CNS and women's health growing ~10-11%, a 34% ROE, no debt, ₹4,238 cr of net cash and a ~2.3% dividend yield, with no royalty to the parent. **What you are not buying:** a pipeline, pricing power, control over the Novo third of revenue, or a management team that talks to investors.

**What you are paying:** ₹27,125 is 35.7x trailing EPS, 34.3x FY27E, 31.4x FY28E and 30.0x Sep-28E: FY28E is 13% below Abbott's 36.1x forward median while pharma peers trade 10.25% above theirs. On the street's method and our (below-consensus) EPS, the house multiple of 40x gives {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): a BUY under our rule. The DCF (₹21,835) says the opposite. The honest reading: the stock is cheap against its own history and its sector, but that history was made while EPS grew ~18% a year; at ~9% the de-rating may be partly deserved (BOBCAPS' 32x, or the midpoint sensitivity at 33.5x, ₹30,320).

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Abbott India (standalone; no subsidiaries; FY = April-March, ₹ crore). One reported segment, so the engine runs one revenue-growth path and one EBITDA-margin path; the business-line build (own brands vs Novo Nordisk partner brands) sits in `businessLines` and the authoring script checks that it sums to model revenue. Other income = treasury yield x opening net cash on the company's basis (cash + all bank term deposits incl. those over 12 months, less lease liabilities: Rs4,238 cr at Mar-26) + recurring non-treasury income. Valued on P/E, as the street does.
assumptions._revenueWhy: Built by business (see businessLines; the script checks the sum). FY27E +5.75%: own brands +11% (Q1FY27 ~+11% on Pharmarack; IQVIA ~12% for the June quarter; most power brands +10-12%; Thyronorm +12.7%, Cremaffin Plus +19.8%, Vertin +18.3%, Influvac +25.2% on MAT Jul-26, but Udiliv +3%, Digene -1%, Duphaston +6% (Pharmarack); price growth limited: NLEM ceiling +0.65% from Apr-2026 on ~26% of the own portfolio) and Novo partner brands -4% (cartridge and pen insulins discontinued from 2025, Mixtard -31% and Rybelsus -16% on MAT Jul-26, partly offset by Extensior from Mar-2026). Q1FY27 was +4.3%; Q2-Q4 at the Q1 run-rate with normal seasonality gives ~Rs7,320 cr. FY28E +7.8%: own +10.5%, partner +2% (Extensior volume, Novo decline annualised). FY29E +7.9%: own +10%, partner +3%. Below the street (BOBCAPS +8% FY27E, ICICI Direct +8%) because we take the Q1 partner decline as lasting.

businessLines._why: Company does not split revenue. FY26 base = 65% own brands / 35% Novo partner brands (BOBCAPS Q4FY26 review: core portfolio 65% of sales; BOBCAPS 3-Sep-2026: in-licensed Novo portfolio 35% of sales; company split FY21-24 was 64-66% / 34-36%). Own brands include services income from Abbott affiliates (Rs81 cr).

assumptions._marginWhy: EBITDA before other income: 26.4% (FY25), 27.3% (FY26), 28.8% in Q1FY27 (gross margin +283bp to 48.6% as low-margin partner sales fell and own brands grew). Mix does most of the work: BOBCAPS puts the core portfolio's EBITDA margin at 41.8% (Q4FY26) against a distribution margin of a few per cent on Novo products, so each point of mix shift adds ~0.4pp. FY27E 28.5%: Q1 28.8%, with Q3 carrying the annual salary cycle (Q3FY26 26.9%) and FY26's labour-code charge (Rs18 cr) not repeating. FY28E 29.0% and FY29E 29.5%: own brands rise from 68% to 71% of revenue; we hold the own-brand margin roughly flat (more launches, field-force investment). BOBCAPS models 28.2/29.2/30.3%, ICICI Direct 27.6/28.1%.
assumptions._capexWhy: Cash capex Rs53 cr (FY25) and Rs41 cr (FY26) plus right-of-use additions (Rs169 cr in FY25 for a new office lease, Rs15 cr in FY26); capital commitments only Rs0.5 cr at Mar-26 (AR FY26 note 37). We use Rs60-65 cr a year including lease additions.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation Rs76 cr (PPE Rs28.7 cr, intangibles Rs2.9 cr, right-of-use Rs44.4 cr); Q1FY27 Rs19.8 cr (Rs79 cr annualised). Rate chosen so FY27E depreciation is ~Rs80 cr on the engine's gross block (CWIP held flat).

otherTreasury._why: Company treasury at Mar-26 = cash and equivalents Rs442.33 cr + term deposits of 3-12 months Rs1,790.00 cr + term deposits with more than 12 months to maturity Rs2,178.00 cr (non-current other financial assets) = Rs4,410.33 cr (AR FY26 notes 6, 10, 11). Screener counts Rs2,254.95 cr as cash (incl. Rs21.28 cr earmarked for unpaid dividends and Rs1.34 cr of margin money) and puts the long deposits in other assets. Adjustment = 2,178.00 - 21.28 - 1.34 = +Rs2,155.38 cr, so the model's opening treasury equals the company's Rs4,410 cr; less Rs172 cr of lease liabilities (Screener borrowings) = Rs4,238 cr of net cash. Interest accrued on deposits (Rs139 cr) is left out.

assumptions._treasuryWhy: FY26 interest on fixed deposits Rs256.75 cr on average deposits and cash of Rs4,098 cr (Mar-25 Rs3,785 cr, Mar-26 Rs4,410 cr) = 6.27% (AR FY26 notes 10-12, 25). Deposits were placed when the repo rate was 6.5%; it was 5.25% when the RBI held it on 5-Aug-2026, so the yield drifts down as one-to-two-year deposits roll over: 6.0% in FY27E, 5.75% after. Applied to opening net cash (the engine has no intra-year timing; the Rs1,394 cr FY26 dividend leaves in Aug-2026 and the engine deducts the FY27 dividend instead, of similar size).
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Recurring non-treasury other income (AR FY26 note 25): steady items ~Rs3 cr (interest on security deposits Rs1.1 cr, rent from an affiliate Rs1.2 cr, other interest and miscellaneous Rs0.7 cr) plus lumpy liabilities written back and insurance/carrier claims (Rs14.8 cr in FY25, Rs12.0 cr in FY26), of which we take about half: ~Rs10 cr a year. Left out as one-offs (Rs16.4 cr in FY26): interest on an income-tax refund Rs10.6 cr, gain on selling two Mumbai offices Rs4.1 cr, exchange gain Rs1.6 cr. FY27E total other income ~Rs264 cr vs Rs288 cr in FY26 and Rs291 cr in the twelve months to Jun-26: the gap is the one-offs, half the lumpy items and the lower deposit yield (6.0% vs 6.27%).
assumptions._interestLabel: Finance cost (interest on lease liabilities, unwinding of provisions)
assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 Rs25.0 cr = lease interest Rs18.0 cr (Rs125 cr of the Rs172 cr lease liability is to Abbott Healthcare for office space) + other Rs2.7 cr + unwinding of provisions Rs4.3 cr; Q1FY27 Rs5.9 cr. Falls as the lease liability amortises. No borrowings.
assumptions._taxWhy: Effective rate 25.4% in FY26 (25.7% before Rs6.8 cr of prior-year credits) and 25.1% in Q1FY27; new-regime 25.17% plus disallowances.
assumptions._payoutWhy: Total payout (final + special) 84.6% / 73.2% / 72.7% / 72.5% / 71.4% / 89.8% in FY21-26: average 77%; the final dividend alone has been ~72% for three years and specials come irregularly (FY26 Rs131 a share). No target payout is disclosed. We use 80%. Timing: the engine deducts each year's dividend in that year; in reality it is paid in August of the next year, so FY27's engine outflow (~Rs1,390 cr) stands in for the Rs1,394 cr FY26 dividend actually paid in Aug-2026.

dcf._betaWhy: Debt-free, cash-rich, India-only branded pharma with an MNC parent: defensive earnings. We keep 0.8 (Ke 11.3%), the same as the other pharma initiations, rather than a lower beta that would flatter the DCF.
dcf._tgWhy: 6%: the Indian pharma market grows ~9-10% in value; Abbott's own brands grow with it, the partner business slower; a long-run nominal rupee growth of 6% is below both.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~8% to 8% (own brands ~10%, partner brands low single digits, mix shifting to own brands).
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: Margin creeps from 29.5% to 30% on mix; no further expansion is assumed (reinvestment in launches and field force).
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex ~1% of revenue (incl. right-of-use additions; FY24-26 average ~0.8% plus leases); depreciation 1.1% of revenue (FY26 1.1%).

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Own brands keep growing at 12-13% (IPM in double digits, Thyronorm, Cremaffin, Vertin, Arachitol and the 75 planned launches), Extensior and Ryzodeg stabilise the partner business, and mix lifts margins faster.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Novo shrinks its Indian portfolio further or ends the arrangement, generics erode Duphaston and Udiliv, and price control caps Thyronorm; revenue grows ~3% a year and margins stall.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How the street values Abbott India: P/E (BOB Capital Markets 32x Sep-28E EPS, 3-Sep-2026; ICICI Direct 36x FY28E, 13-Aug-2026; ICICI Securities 38x FY27E, Nov-2025). 40x = Abbott's 36.1x median one-year-forward P/E since Apr-2021 (house forwardMedian on reported EPS; exceptional items are immaterial, so the pre-exceptional median is also 36.1x; no trough years: forward EPS was never below 108.3% of its prior three-year peak) times the pharma sector factor of 1.1025 (median of SUNPHARMA, DIVISLAB, TORNTPHARM, ZYDUSLIFE, CIPLA, AUROPHARMA, ALKEM, IPCALAB trailing P/E at the 30-Sep close vs their five-year medians: +10.25%, PLAYBOOK §7c; our reproduction +10.25%) = 39.8x, rounded to the nearest half-turn. No blend with Abbott's own de-rating (−25.6%) and no growth adjustment (sensitivity rows only). Bull 43x (75th percentile 39.1x x factor); bear 37.5x (25th percentile 34.1x x factor).

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Counts net cash at face value and ignores other income. Abbott's own trailing EV/EBITDA since Apr-2021 (market value less company net cash incl. long deposits, over operating EBITDA before other income; Screener's series includes other income and ignores long deposits) has a median of 36.0x; times the EV/EBITDA analogue of the sector factor (+9.1%, same eight peers) = 39.3x, rounded to 39.5x and applied to trailing EBITDA at the target date (half FY27E + half FY28E) plus net cash at Sep-2027. Bull 41.5x / bear 37x (75th / 25th percentile x factor).

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 15-year FCFF at an 11.3% cost of equity, terminal growth 6%, plus net cash.
